Each run fills the metrics table in the runbook: time to detect, attribute and respond; chain completeness; detection rate; false positives against the scorer and against our own hardening [RT]. These are measured and reported, not targets (decision 9).

**The C2 fingerprinting lab** (review D76, D222, A6.Q4; see T60). It stands up the common C2 frameworks, captures their traffic, and turns the results into rules. The frameworks are: Mythic (Apollo and Poseidon agents with a Gaia redirector), Sliver, Havoc, Metasploit, Empire, Realm `imix`, and the tunnels chisel, ligolo-ng, frp and ngrok. Cobalt Strike is covered through public malleable profiles and pcaps only. For each framework and one customised profile, capture at the implant host (the `capture` module) and at the sinkhole: the first bytes of each direction, TLS fingerprints (JA4), HTTP request shape, beacon interval and jitter, and on Windows the named pipes (Sysmon 17 and 18). The **decision rule** it exists for: keep the sinkhole if a rule on the first bytes of a connection identifies a framework's default captures and matches nothing in the benign corpus (the scorer's captures, the Orange traffic and ordinary browsing); otherwise cut the sinkhole code. The exact threshold for "identifies" (how many frameworks must be separable) is for David to confirm; the code stays until the lab has run. Real captures from the Invitational (observe items R4 and R8) can seed the benign and attack corpora.

**Prebaked set.**

- **Linux:** cron, timers and a firewall-disabling timer; `update-motd`; a PAM backdoor module; `ld.so.preload`; PHP `auto_prepend_file`; a Postfix pipe transport; alternate-path `authorized_keys`; a SUID shell; LKM and eBPF rootkit samples (lab only). From the coverage spec [COV §5]: a replaced Postfix `smtpd` proxying to a second lab host; an apache or httpd unit with `Environment=LD_PRELOAD` and `AmbientCapabilities`; a PHP extension that overrides `disable_functions`; `chattr +i` on a unit and a sudoers.d file; a bind mount over a webroot directory; `apt-mark hold libpam-modules`; a `.screenrc` hook; a `PROMPT_COMMAND` callback; `nologin` replaced by a bash copy; NTP and DNS TXT covert-channel traffic; a self-propagating SSH key installer; a defanged cron wiper; a backdoor inside an existing core file (`framework.php` style); an extra `oc_user` row.
- **Windows:** a firewall-disabling scheduled task; a service in a writable path; a WMI subscription; an IFEO debugger; an LSA package; a Run key; a hidden admin; `dns.exe` replaced with a forwarding stub and command listener; the FTP root pointing at an SMB share; `LSASS` to `ISASS.EXE`; a hijacked `\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting` task; a Mythic-style unsigned SYSTEM service; WSL and Chocolatey launch; an OpenSSH server and a VNC listener.
- **AD:** an extra Domain Admin and a nested fake group inside Enterprise Admins; an SPN on a user; RBCD; a GPO immediate task; a DCSync ACE; `ServerLevelPluginDll`; a Defender exclusion; audit policy off; organizer-style "temp admins" and secrets in user descriptions.
- **Network:** a VyOS task-scheduler script; an extra Palo admin; a Palo allow rule above a block rule; a custom admin role.

Dropped from v3's set because the capability is cut or absent from 2027: the promiscuous NIC (rule D19 is cut) and the IIS native module (IIS is not in the 2027 environment).

**Comms bench.** David asked (2026-11-06) for the communications path to be measured before the Invitational and again at it, with the same numbers, so the two compare. Two parts, one record format (`docs/impl/14-bench.md`). The **live recorder** is part of the controller, on by default in every mode including observe mode: every 10 s it appends one JSONL record for the controller and one per agent to `<data_dir>/bench.jsonl` (rotated at `bench_max_mb`, 64 by default, one previous file kept): events and JSON bytes per second by priority class, event-to-controller latency per class (controller commit time minus the event time corrected by the agent's heartbeat clock skew), SQLite commit time, gap records and reconnects with the disconnected time, controller CPU and RSS, store size, the timing of the Overview, Health and event queries the UI uses, and per agent the heartbeat round trip, ack lag, spool depth and congestion state, clock skew and the per-module usage the heartbeat carries (`cpu_ms`, `held_bytes`, `events`, `bytes_out`, `dropped`). Latencies are fixed 1-2-5 millisecond histograms, so percentiles over any window stay exact to the bucket and 10 000 ms is a bucket edge. `phylax bench report <file>` prints the tables. The **lab load generator**, `phylax bench load -lab`, runs N synthetic agents (the real agent runtime, spool and link, enrolled with real tokens through a proxy it can cut) at configured events per second per class against a lab controller, cuts the link for 60 s, restores it, and checks the four criteria the transport envelope gives (p99 at most 10 s outside the outage and its recovery; no gap or shed events after 60 s; one reconnect per agent within 35 s; the spool drains). The lab task also repeats the cut on the real agents with a firewall drop. Pass criteria are the envelope; everything else is measured and reported (decision 9).

### Test matrix

**This section owns the list of test ids.** Module sections, the risk table, the simulators and the CI section cite ids from this matrix and define none of their own. The ids are stable. v3's ids T01 to T45 keep their numbers, because module sections and the review cite them; renumbering after the cuts would break those citations (this overrides the review's D514 request to renumber, which would have cost every citation for no gain). Three ids are retired and never reused: T04 (ASPX webshell on IIS), T26 (Windows raw-socket capture) and T42 (Sigma import). New tests continue from T46 and run to T81, 36 tests (T77 to T79 are the A-AUTO and B1 tests; T80 and T81 are the comms bench). Every id from T01 to T81 is either in the two tables below or retired. Latencies in the "pass when" column are **measured and reported**, not targets (decision 9); where v3 gave a time, the run records it and compares it with the last release. The design envelope for transport (10 s event-to-controller while the link is up; outages up to 60 s) is a sizing figure, not a goal.

Bugs 3, 10 and 11 have no regression test of their own: bug 3 is a deletion with no behaviour left to test, bug 10 is reference data that manifest CI covers by rendering the reference manifest with its scored DNS and FTP services, and bug 11 is guarded by the CI check "Known bug 11 guard" rather than a regression test |
| T66 | Pass-the-hash pack with the scorer's NTLM baseline (A7.Q7) | The scorer's NTLM and Kerberos logins raise nothing; the same account used from a non-scorer source raises the alert |
| T67 | Per-executable egress allowlist (A1, A6.Q3) | Alert-only for a program outside the allowlist; the one-click "block this?" suggestion creates a plan; nothing blocks silently |
| T68 | Opt-in `noexec` remount of temp directories | The pre-check refuses when a scored service execs from there; a live remount rolls back on failure |
| T69 | Inventory snapshots, `probe.run`, drift adoption and the version matcher | Differential snapshots report added, removed and changed rows; a probe returns typed output; adopt writes to overrides and revert is a plan; a KEV fixture matches an installed version |
| T70 | Observe mode (Invitational configuration) | With every module alert-only and safe mode on, host state before and after a full run is identical apart from three listed exceptions: the agent, the `decoys` module's listeners and the honeytoken files it plants (`file.plant`); no other firewall, account, service or file change |
| T71 | Module usage: self-reported against measured | The ratio of each module's reported CPU and held bytes to the cgroup or Job Object figure is reported (open question 9); no threshold yet |
| T72 | Reboot-survival preflight (hardening) | A change that would stop the host booting is flagged before apply; one that survives is not |
| T73 | Controller executor, approval classes and standing approvals (builder check) | `Host.RunReadOnly` refuses a plan with a node that has `Touches`, a risk above `none` or no `ReadOnly` flag (rule `SS000`); a standing approval covers a backup dump inside its scope and refuses one outside it, after its expiry, and any `lockout`, `destructive` or `host.exec` node; a `creds` plan is never started without a click except the `resync` re-apply; an `auto` plan (A-AUTO) starts only from an allowlisted template, is refused when it holds a `destructive`, `proc.kill_tree`, krbtgt, device-revert or whole-service-restore node or when its probe cannot run (it becomes a click proposal), rolls back on a failed after-probe and halts its template after two rollbacks in 10 minutes; a controller-local action (`suricata.analyze_pcap`) runs in the controller executor with the same locks, lint and audit |
| T74 | Controller facts (builder check) | A `control: fact` reaches the agent bus as `controller.fact` and is not spooled; a fact with an expired `ttl` or none received is unknown, and `respond` makes no tier-0 action and proposes tier 1 instead; a later fact with the same id replaces the earlier one; a `work_window` fact stamps the envelope `Tag` and ends at `until` with the link down; a `creds_txn` fact pauses a runner's checks for that account |
| T75 | Canonical fields and replay (builder check) | Every producer's fixture events of a common kind decode strictly against the canonical struct (`conn` from `audit`, `winevt`, `net`, `capture`; `file_change`; `auth_event`; `listener`; `process_start`); the rule loader rejects a field outside the struct; a `replay: true` event never enters a `count`, `sequence` or `jitter` window or a rule without `replay: allow`; a canary event is exempt by `canary: true` and the envelope `Tag` stays empty |
| T76 | Release signatures and enrollment package (builder check) | A release artifact signed by `internal/signing` verifies with plain `ssh-keygen -Y verify`; a tampered artifact fails; plan and config signing still verifies under its own scheme and rejects an sshsig signature; `internal/enroll` push, one-liner and token consumption pass their tests, and a module importing it fails the sibling-import check |
| T77 | Inbound firewall enforcement and allow-back (A-AUTO) | A host enforced inbound-only drops an unlisted port, keeps scored ports, management, dependency and learned flows, leaves outbound in shadow; a planted scorer-like probe to an unrendered port is allowed back within seconds with `firewall.allow_back`; a forced failure rolls back through the dead-man; no `out_mode: enforce` runs without the outbound gate click |
| T78 | AD Recycle Bin (B1) | `ad.recycle_enable` checks the functional level first and is idempotent; deleting a scored user on the lab DC triggers D7h and the user returns with the same password hash and groups, verified by a scorer login; a user deleted before enablement is flagged, not re-created |
| T79 | Automatic default (A-AUTO) | An `auto` plan starts from an allowlisted pack, applies behind the probe and rolls back on a forced red probe; the template halts after two rollbacks; with the link down or no probe the same plan is a click proposal; `proc.kill_tree`, krbtgt, device revert and whole-service restore never run unattended; a rule promoted to `act` through `rule_modes` acts and a demotion stops it; the content guard promotes a service after a clean shadow period and demotes it on a stop |
| T80 | Comms bench: recorder, report and RTT (builder check) | With a real controller and real agents the recorder writes one `ctl` and one `agent` record per interval to `bench.jsonl` (on by default, `bench_off` disables it), carrying per-class events, bytes and event-to-commit latency histograms, store commit time, gap and reconnect counts, controller CPU and RSS, store size, query times, and per agent the heartbeat RTT, lag, spool depth, congestion and per-module usage; the file never exceeds twice `bench_max_mb`; `phylax bench report` prints the percentile tables and ignores a torn last line; a heartbeat's echoed `ack` yields a round-trip time and a stale echo yields none |
| T81 | Comms bench: load and 60 s partition on the replica (lab) | `phylax bench load` with N synthetic agents (real `agent` and `spool` code, enrolled with real tokens) at configured rates per class, plus the real agents on the stack: p99 event-to-commit at most 10 s outside the partition and its recovery; after a 60 s partition zero gap events and zero shed events, each agent reconnects once within 35 s of restore and its spool drains; the numbers are recorded in `docs/impl/lab/w14-bench.md` next to the live recording from the Invitational and compared. All other figures (RTT, bytes per second, module CPU and held bytes, commit time, query latency, agents per controller before the envelope is missed) are measured and reported |
| T82 | Tag scope (R6): all red activity is seen and some blue can be shown as red, not the other way around | With a plan step running and a work window open on the same host, a process that is not a descendant of the step's child is untagged and alerts; a webshell child, an `auth_event`, an egress connection and a honeytoken read during a window alert as if untagged; a `file_change` by the claimed user inside the window and the step's own child processes are tagged and exempt; a changed system clock neither extends nor ends a window early. Every red fixture alerts; blue fixtures may alert; no red fixture is silenced by a tag |
| T83 | Controller disk quotas (R9) | With the data disk driven to 90, 95 and 98% full: bulk events and bulk transfers are refused at 90%, alert evidence and pcap slices also at 95%, and only high and critical events are accepted at 98%; alerts are never shed; a refused run is recorded as one skipped run (shown as a gap), the chain continues over it and the agent's spool drains; safe mode and the kill switch work with the audit write failing; a flooding agent cannot fill the disk past the thresholds; `store.quota` fires at each crossing |
| T84 | Controller restore epoch and locked controller (R7, R8) | Restoring twice from the same snapshot produces epoch `max(snapshot, reported)+1` the second time and agents accept it; a restarted controller with signing locked emits `controller.locked`, the Overview shows the LOCKED banner, the snapshot writer reports "skipped: locked", and a plan resumes after unlock |
| T85 | Console-script enrollment checks (R1) | A binary whose hash differs from the one served raises `enroll.hash_mismatch`; a bundled host that does not connect inside the window raises `enroll.no_show`; a refused enrollment raises an alert-class `enroll.refused`; `<host>.json` is gone from the served directory after that host connects; bundles are not served outside the window |
| T86 | Per-host act and safe mode (R2) | An `act` entry for `respond` on one canary host acts there and nowhere else; `safe_mode_hosts` holds exactly those hosts in safe mode across a reconnect; `detect` alerts keep their rule mode with `detect.act_enabled` false and `respond.act_enabled` true on the host |
| T87 | Probe inside the node and the busy answer (R12) | A pack whose second node breaks a scored path with the link up is rolled back by the agent because `deadman_confirm` waits for the after-probe; a plan that touches a scored service gets `rollback_plan` by default; one before-probe and one after-probe per host and phase for nodes sharing a lock set; a ninth concurrent step is answered `busy`, retried, and does not trigger `on_failure` |

### CI

The privileged job and `-race` are required checks on every push and pull request (review D515, D516). A required job does not skip: a test that needs privileges, containers or SQL Server skips with a clear message in a developer's shell (repo `AGENTS.md`), but the CI job that provides them fails if any of its tests skipped.

- **Static builds** for both OSes with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, linux/amd64 and windows/amd64, a size check (40 MB, 15 MB compressed), `make vet` for both, signed artifacts. `GOOS=windows go build` is a required job.
- **`go test -race ./...`** on every package (T45).
- **Module contract.** The conformance suite (T46); `go list -deps` per module package against the allowed set (no sibling imports); config schema generation checked against the Go structs; the declared-kind registry check; the rule-id registry check; the Typst and `rules/imported/` references check (none may remain).
- **A privileged job** runs `nft -c`, AF_PACKET, systemd D-Bus and SELinux-enforcing container tests, and the database round trips against real MySQL and MariaDB containers.
- **Unit tests for every action** (check, apply, verify, rollback) against Rocky, Ubuntu and Debian containers, and Windows runners.
- **Parser and normalizer tests** from recorded captures, including the Quotient pcaps from the lab; fuzzing for every parser, the fake shell, the prompt extractor and the Markdown subset parser.
- **Rule tests.** Every rule has inline fixtures; ATT&CK ids are validated against the pinned v19 dataset.
- **Manifest tests.** Schema, cycles, the firewall lint, rendering of every output for the reference manifest, and a lint that every plan template passes the scoring-safety rules.
- **UI tests** for escaping (T25) and for the authentication surface (T28).
- **Cache build** job and an offline-sync smoke test.
- **Known bug 11 guard.** A check that every `t.Skip` in non-privileged code carries a `shortcut:` or a reason string.
- **Package done** (builder check). A package (a module's retrofit or a core package) is done when CI is green (both OSes build, `make vet`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`) and the package has unit, fixture and conformance tests that exercise the real code. Lab tests are a separate gate, run by a stronger agent or by David (Lab-first acceptance), and a package can be done without being lab-proven.

### Lab questions and where they get answered

The open lab questions are listed under Risks and open questions, each with the lab test or Invitational observation that answers it. The Invitational (`docs/impl/invitational-data.md`) answers many of them with real data: S1 and S2 for the round clock (T30), S3 for the Palo source-address question, S5 and S6 for scorer accounts and NTLM against Kerberos (T50, T66), S9 for scorer session length (T49), E8 for Windows defence and logging state (T24, T27), E12 for the Palo licence, E14 for controller headroom, R4 for C2 captures (T60), O1 and O2 for console bootstrap and usability (T27), O3 for module costs (T71), O4 for Defender (T24), O8 for the time to type a PCR list (T35), O9 for restore sizes (T53). Its collectors are standalone scripts and Phylax in observe mode, so nothing there changes the repository.

### Cadence

This is a cadence, not a deadline.

- A weekly purple-team session on one campaign; the runbook's metrics table is filled in after each run [RT].
- A 24-hour soak test per release on the full lab.
- A monthly full dry run with all simulators and fault injection.
- Two full dry runs in competition roles in the final three weeks before each major event, with timestamps recorded so the runs can be compared.

## Complexity register

One line per module (all 34), plus the core items. Each line says why the complexity earns its place and what bounds it. Any new listener, daemon, host-binary dependency in a default path, runtime discovery mechanism or new kind of state needs a line before it is built.

| Item | Why it is worth it | How it is bounded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One binary for agent and controller | One artifact per OS; no version skew | Size gate in CI |
| Relay and device-proxy splicing | Segments and devices the controller cannot reach | Dumb splice, no state, no keys; declared statically; unused on the 2027 LAN |
| Four connection types on one port | One listener and one firewall rule | Small handler per ALPN; UI on a separate localhost listener |
| Kali inbound path (one port, one source, static NAT) | The only way for an outside vantage point to report | One Palo rule, one host rule, Kali source only, pinned keys |
| Module contract (registry, typed events, conformance suite) | Makes the platform's size and isolation checkable | One small package; CI enforces it |
| Dead-man with OS timers | Risky changes roll back even if the agent dies | Journal plus one transient timer per armed node |
| Shared stateless libraries (`internal/checks/probe`, `internal/sockets`, `internal/signing` and others) | Several modules need one probe, socket reader or signer without importing each other | A closed list checked in CI; a library that grows state, events or goroutines becomes a module |
| Plan expiry (`expires_after`) | Time-boxed allowances end even if the controller dies | The dead-man's armed record and one-shot timer with the confirm step turned off; no new daemon |
| Lint registry | Modules add scoring-safety rules (`DEP001`, the PCR transaction rule) without a core package depending on a module | One id namespace, a registry test, inline tests per rule |
| Signed `control: fact` messages (subtypes `work_window`, `round_clock`, `gpo_finding`, `scorer_probe_result`, `creds_txn`) and the `controller.fact` bus kind | Tagged windows, the quiet-window gate and cross-host guard inputs reach agents with the link as the only channel, through one mechanism | Small signed messages with a `ttl`, a closed subtype table, delivered to the bus only (never spooled), absence is unknown and unknown means do not act |
| Controller executor, approval classes (`click`, `auto_readonly`, `standing`, `auto`) and `Host.RunReadOnly`, `Host.RunStanding`, `Host.RunAuto`, `Host.Control` | Controller-local actions and scheduled work (backup dumps, hunt repeats, the AD baseline) need to run without a click per run, and (A-AUTO) the automatic default needs plans that start themselves behind probes | Same action contract and lint; `auto_readonly` only for `ReadOnly` actions with no `Touches` (rule `SS000`); a standing approval has scope, an operator, an expiry and never covers `lockout`, `destructive` or `host.exec`; `auto` only for allowlisted templates whose nodes are all reversible and probed, with a per-template circuit breaker, and never for the click-only set |
| Comms bench (`internal/bench`: the live recorder, `phylax bench report`, `phylax bench load`) | The communications path is measured before and at the Invitational with the same numbers | Controller-local, one bounded JSONL file (64 MB, one previous file kept), no host state, no module; the load generator is lab-only |
| `internal/enroll` (SSH and WinRM push, one-liner, bootstrap handler, tokens) | First contact is one core path with one set of failure classes | Core package, not importable by modules; protocol clients come from the shared probe library |
| sshsig release signatures | A release verifies with plain `ssh-keygen` and no phylax binary | One release key; plan and config signing keeps its own domain-separated scheme |
| Canonical field tables for the common kinds, `evidence.blob` | Rules cover Linux and Windows with one condition; alert evidence has one transfer path | Conformance decodes producer fixtures strictly; 8 MiB per item and 64 MiB per alert |
| Go-native Windows actions through COM and WMI | Avoids trusting host binaries | `host.exec` fallback per action, recorded here |
| Field-level encryption of captured credentials | No plaintext passwords on the controller's disk | Parsers mark credential fields |
| Defender exclusion | The agent may be flagged | Exactly one path |
| `validate` hook validators as host tools | Catch a broken config before it is live | Services' own binaries, hash-pinned, ledger-judged |
| Obscurity measures | Raise the cost of scripted kill lists | Names and paths only; no mutated binaries |
| `audit` | The only source of argv, parent and user in one record, and it keeps recording when the agent is killed | Fixed rule set rendered from config, a guard that repairs only its own `phylax`-keyed rules, a throttled hash sweep, every loss reported as a `telemetry_gap`; no eBPF sensor |
| `winevt` | The Windows process, auth and persistence facts all come from one subscription layer; Sysmon is the only per-process network and DNS source | Bookmarked `EvtSubscribe` channels from a fixed list, the Sysmon config embedded and hash-checked, 4688 as the fallback |
| `net` | Owning process for listeners and denied egress is what turns a firewall log into a C2 lead | A 2 s poll, a bounded connection table, canary dials only to destinations policy blocks, Linux only until the Windows half is built |
| `logs` | The only source of Linux authentication facts, and the scorer-versus-attacker line depends on them | Parsers are YAML with inline tests, per-file rate limits and offsets, no log is read that a parser does not name |
| `inventory` | Drift, the hunt's reference diff and the version matcher share one collection instead of three | Epoch plus diff, at most 500 rows per event, read-only probes, off unless enabled |
| `detect` | One rule engine on the host keeps detection alive with the link down | A declarative language with no expressions, 10 ms/s of CPU, a global alert-only override, per-rule alert-to-act promotion on evidence (A-AUTO), rules without a test fail CI |
| `respond` | Tier-0 restores of the firewall, Defender and audit within seconds are the lab's success metric, and (A-AUTO) acting automatically is the default | Recipes allowlisted per host, `act_enabled` off in code, a circuit breaker per action type and per auto template, loop detection, time-boxed and capped automatic blocks, a click-only set, safe mode stops it |
| `content_guard` | Scored content tampering is the most-scored class and a golden copy is the fastest fix | Opt-in per service, six constraints, shadow first and automatic after a clean shadow period (A-AUTO), a second restore within 10 minutes stops it |
| `integrity` | A replaced binary is invisible to every behavioural rule | Alert only, never restores by itself, ledger from off-host sources, throttled sweeps, a pinned YARA-X |
| `hunt` | Prebaked implants are not changes, so no change detector sees them | Read-only collectors, a 10-minute interval, a review queue, findings end in disable and quarantine, never delete |
| `hardening` | Repeatable, probed hardening without new Go | Plan content over core actions, every pack passes the scoring lint, automatic start only on probe-before green with auto-rollback (A-AUTO), reboot gates stay a click, one new action (`mount.remount`), reboot-survival preflight |
| `ad` | The DC is the worst case to lose and the hardest to harden by hand | Agent on the DC plus a small controller side (baseline trigger, `gpo_finding` fact), one `ADBackend` interface with a fake, `report_only` options, `krbtgt` reset needs `confirm` and a click, the Recycle Bin enable is the one accepted one-way action and is guarded by a forest-level check (B1), the GPO unlink is automatic with rollback (A-AUTO) |
| `firewall` | Default-deny egress and drift restore need a manager that can prove a policy before enforcing it, and inbound default-deny (automatic, A-AUTO) removes lateral paths | Shadow before outbound enforce, inbound enforced behind the probe, the dead-man and an automatic allow-back, scored ports never narrowed, foreign tables reported not touched |
| `egress` | The first denied outbound connection from a server is the primary C2 signal | A pure analyser, no actions of its own, suggestions are one-click proposals and outbound enforcement is a click after review (A-AUTO), the sinkhole stays deferred |
| `capture` | Frozen packet evidence and the scorer's request features exist nowhere else | Linux only, ring and hold in the heap under a configured budget, parsers isolated and fuzzed, drops before slowing the host |
| `devices` | Palo and VyOS tamper detection and safe change from the console-free side | Device-side revert (commit confirm, soft-revert), read-only pollers, additive management edits, controller-side only |
| `checks` | The only way to see the scorer's view of a service before the scorer does | The scorer's own client libraries, a login-rate bound, a target allowlist, quiet-window gating |
| `scorer` | Quotient is unreachable from inside, so its clock and accounts must be learned | Estimates carry confidence, hand-entered scoreboard notes outrank probes for the rounds they name, no portal polling |
| `vantage` | Only a Kali outside the Palo sees the public path the scorer uses | One inbound path, an allowlist of targets, a connect scan at a bounded rate, memory-only credentials |
| `creds` | A scored-password change without a plan breaks scoring or leaks the list | A typed PCR list a human enters, revert re-sync (the host-side re-apply is automatic, A-AUTO), no submit, the lint exception keyed by transaction id |
| `traceback` | Every IR needs a cause and a source address | An analyser over stored events, no live state, labels are events |
| `chains` | Half of the IR rubric is remediation of the attack path | Rows and linking rules, no graph engine, per-hop confidence and link method |
| `deps` | Default-deny egress needs the dependencies a service really has | A learning window, proposals not applied, Linux collector first, lint rules registered not hard-wired |
| `vuln` | The CVE table inject and version-driven mitigation | Offline KEV cache, `unknown` for backports, opt-in |
| `decoys` | A cheap early signal from the first thing red touches | LAN only, never on a scored port, unprivileged process, hostile-input parsers fuzzed |
| `honeytokens` | High-confidence critical signals from credentials and files red takes | A registry of generated values, planted only where declared, never on scored content paths |
| `report` | IR and inject artifacts are scored work | Generators render facts, no prewritten responses, pure-Go PDF, files secondary to the screen |
| `backup` | A restore after destruction is the only recovery from razing | Tool hashes pinned, counts before and after, a loss gate with a named approval, a golden gate; `backup` never restores scored users: the Recycle Bin restore of a deleted scored user is `ad`'s automatic restore (B1, `ad.recycle_restore`) and sets no password |
| `teamfeed` | Hand work needs a tagged window or it alarms the whole team | Text only, a root-only local endpoint, short visible windows |
| `notify` | One screen needs an attention channel | Webhook carries only title, severity and host, a blocked webhook never delays the alarm |
| `depot` | Offline-first installs and tools | One signed index with a priority field, hash-verified blobs, no automatic package rollback |
| `wazuh` | Optional OSS sensor the team may run alongside | Pinned fixed version, active response off, a kill-and-skip option |
| `splunk` | Optional forwarding to the scored Splunk's own tooling | In-memory queue, best effort, never touches an existing index, token, search or role |
| `suricata` | Optional offline signature context on frozen pcaps | Runs unprivileged on a copy of the pcap, one pcap at a time, flags asserted by a test |

### Watch list

- Any second listener on the controller beyond `agent_port` and the localhost UI, or any listener on a host that is not a declared decoy, relay or Kali-path port.
- `host.exec` creeping into default plans.
- Rules or parsers that need state shared across hosts at the agent. Cross-host logic belongs on the controller.
- Configuration that can be changed on hosts without going through the manifest.
- A feature that needs a live internet fetch at the event.
- A module that imports a sibling, or a controller feature that is still a method on `Controller` after its area is implemented.
- Anything that makes the integrity ledger act without a human.

## Risks and open questions

The largest risks are the unknown Quotient configuration, the controller as the single root of trust, the T+0 console phase being manual and the first thing red attacks, the amount of Windows work, and the unverified paths that files and sound need to leave the controller. The v3 risk about schedule against scope stays, with the v4 change that scope is not cut for time (decision D-6 replaced).

### Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scope is large and no accepted item is cut for time | High | High | Dependency-first sequencing (module contract and bus first, then retrofit); every gate usable on its own; hand playbooks as the fallback for any event before a gate; a module without evidence starts off; no scope change without the owner |
| Controller compromised | Low | Critical | Separate authenticated UI listener, one inbound agent port, SSH off, secrets in memory, separate signing key |
| Controller lost | Medium | High | Encrypted snapshots every 15 min; drill T23 |
| Quotient's real configuration differs from the reconstruction (Delay, SLA, custom scripts, Divisor, debug, credlist count) | High | Medium | Every model parameter is estimated from capture at the event; defaults held at low confidence; measured at the Invitational (S1 to S9). Quotient is not reachable from inside, so there is no portal poll to fall back on; an optional hand-entered Up/Down note is advisory only |
| Our scorer-mimic probes diverge from the real checks | Medium | High | Same client libraries; lab ground truth through the Quotient admin API (T39); union plus faithful modes; calibrate against the hand-entered Up/Down note and the organizers' post-event check log |
| A hardening plan breaks a scored check | Medium | High | The lint (including never narrowing sources on a scored port), the probe before and after, rollback, the golden restore |
| A scored-password change fails a user for several rounds | Medium | Medium | Quiet-window rule; Kali verification and the scorer's next login; rollback by a typed list of the old values; scored changes happen only on evidence (decision 5) |
| A typo in the typed PCR list at the Quotient machine | Medium | Medium | A short list (credlist, user, password) from `pcr.generate`; the human check on screen; verification by login per credlist; the rollback list is printed with it; the typing time is measured (O8) |
| Red dumps every AD hash and a Phylax breach exposes every rotated password | Medium | High | Prevent the dump (Zerologon first at T+0, the DCSync rule); honey AD accounts; pass-the-hash pack; selective rotation on evidence; rotated scored passwords live in the age vault; policy is open question 1 |
| T+0 console rotation is wrong or late: team-pack admin passwords leak within seconds | High | High | Rehearsed (T48); a printed sheet generated from the manifest; the grid records who did each step; Phylax's first job afterwards is to evict interactive sessions that predate the rotation; Zerologon is done before any domain rotation; only the interactive admin identities' default passwords are rotated, so no scored service can be taken down by the T+0 phase |
| The Invitational's console scripts fetch the kit, the binary and a host's bundle over plain HTTP, so a party on the segment can swap the binary or enroll as a host | Medium | Medium | Detection, not a pin (the typed line is too short for one): the agent reports its own binary hash in `hello` and the controller alerts on a mismatch with what it served; alerts on a bundled host that never connects and on a refused enrollment; bundles served only during enrollment and removed once the host connects (R1; T85). Accepted residual risk: a trojan that lies about its own hash. The pinned one-liner is the production path |
| The controller restarts with nobody at the console and plan signing stays locked | Medium | High | Critical alarm and a LOCKED banner (R8); the dead-man stays fail-safe, so in-flight changes roll back; the snapshot writer reports "skipped: locked" from the same flag (T84) |
| The controller disk fills during a flood | Medium | High | Hard quotas with a fixed shed order (bulk at 90%, evidence and normal events at 95%, high and critical only at 98%), alerts never shed, safe mode and the kill switch exempt from the audit-write refusal (R9; T83) |
| A host or the AD is reverted and Quotient keeps the new passwords | Medium | High | Revert detection and a per-credlist re-sync that blocks further scored changes on that host until resolved (T51) |
| The Kali is in the red team's reach or cannot run our agent | Medium | Medium | In-LAN runners and passive logic work without it; its credentials are memory-only; its verdicts are treated as external-view evidence only |
| Controller DHCP address changes, breaking the Palo NAT target for the Kali | Medium | Medium | Hold or request a reservation; `set-controller`; manual NAT edit; Kali features degrade only |
| Go-native Windows work (COM, WMI, `EvtSubscribe`) takes longer than planned | High | Medium | `host.exec` fallback per action, each recorded in the complexity register; Windows gates in the lab matrix |
| SChannel cannot complete the PowerShell bootstrap | Medium | High | ECDSA P-256 everywhere; T27 early |
| Defender flags the agent | Medium | High | Lab test per release (T24); one scoped exclusion; randomised path |
| The Palo rewrites source addresses on inbound NAT | Medium | High | Detected at the first look (Invitational S3); sources recovered from the Palo's traffic logs; traffic labels work by behaviour, never address |
| The PAN-OS lab VM is unlicensed and behaves differently from the event's | Medium | High | Test on the lab VM early (T44); the adapter reads the licence and disables actions that need subscriptions |
| Integrity ledger false positives from patch drift | Medium | Medium | Truth sources off-host; `match_other_version`; window tags; accept-hash queue; first-sweep unknowns go to the hunt's triage queue, not to alerts |
| Chain mislinks present guesses as facts | Medium | Medium | Per-hop confidence and link method; exact-tuple first; guessed hops labelled in the IR |
| Cache incomplete or stale at the event | Medium | Medium | One signed index with a priority field; offline drill T40; features show "waiting" |
| Wazuh manager exposure or resource starvation | Medium | Medium | Pinned fixed version, host choice by measurement, active response off, kill-and-skip option |
| Obscurity breaks our own detections or hunts | Low | Low | The controller knows the per-event names; detections key on path and hash |
| Red team reads the repo and tunes around detections | High | Medium | Behavioural and allowlist detections; per-event values generated at the event; lab payloads and campaign runbooks kept in the private repo |
| Telemetry loss hides an attack | Medium | High | `telemetry_gap` events, the health block, cross-source tripwires, load test T43 |
| The platform driver becomes the bottleneck on the one controller screen | Medium | Medium | Dry runs; pre-built plans; the role-merge map; `phylax say` and `claim`; the `notify` alarm and webhook; the "since you left" digest. No SSH tunnel (A11.Q1) |
| Files and sound cannot leave the controller: Nextcloud not writable from inside, no audio in NETLAB | Medium | Medium | The on-screen views are the primary artifact and screenshot from the console; files stay on controller disk and are carried out later; the visual alarm and banner work without sound; both paths are checked at the Invitational |
| A claimed work window hides attacker activity | Medium until built (R6), then Low | Medium | Windows tag only change-class events of the claimed session or user, never process, network, authentication or honeytoken events; scored-service rules ignore tags; the end is a monotonic duration; windows are short, visible on the Overview and in the audit log (the `teamfeed` section; T82) |
| The content guard fights an inject that changes the same content, or loops | Low | Medium | Off by default per service; plan-tagged changes exempt; a second restore within 10 minutes stops and alerts (T52) |
| A restore loses data (a per-user penalty) | Low | High | Counts before and after; the loss gate needs a named approval; a pre-change set is taken first (T53) |
| An automatic action (A-AUTO) breaks a scored service or locks out a scored user | Medium | High | The default is to act, so the safety net is structural: scorer-mimic probe before and after, auto-rollback and the dead-man, a circuit breaker per action type and per auto template, loop detection, time-boxed and capped automatic blocks, a click-only set (process-tree kills, scored-password changes, destructive or one-way actions, any action whose probe cannot run), per-rule mode promotion on Invitational data, `act_enabled` off in code and in the Invitational reference manifest, safe mode |
| Inbound default-deny drops a scorer check before the allow-back lands (A-AUTO) | Low | Medium | The allow set is rendered from the manifest (scored ports any source, `FW101`), learned scorer listeners join it, the apply runs behind the probe and the dead-man, and the allow-back restores a scored or scorer-like port within seconds; at most one check on that port can fail; the lab test T77 measures it |
| A deleted scored user that is not in the Recycle Bin (deleted before enablement) cannot be restored with its hash (B1) | Low | High | The bin is enabled automatically in the first-hour automation on the DC (forest functional level checked first), so the window is the minutes before enablement; such a case is flagged to an operator and `backup` never creates a scored password |
| Razing: the host does not boot after a deleted boot file | Medium | High | Fresh `boot` sets before lunch and before day 2; the boot-critical watchlist; console recovery rehearsed (T55) |
| A module breaks the contract during the retrofit and drags the platform | Medium | Medium | Modules show as "pre-contract" until retrofitted; the conformance suite and the sibling-import check are required in CI (T46) |
| Per-module CPU and memory are self-reported and may be wrong | Medium | Low | The whole process is capped by the OS (systemd, Job Object); T71 compares the report with measurement |
| No PAN-OS or Windows licences in the lab for some variants | Medium | Medium | Evaluation licences requested early |
| Containerised scored services in 2027 behave differently from the Docker variant | Medium | Medium | The `runtime` field and the variant host (T63); the stack is unverified until a packet shows it |

### Open questions

Open questions that are genuinely open (not decided anywhere):

1. **Scored-password policy against full AD dumps** (review A7.Q6). Red dumps every AD hash, and a Phylax breach exposes every rotated password. The PCR process stays (selective, timed, verified, revert re-apply); research on how Quotient-region teams handle this is running.
2. **`pcr.submit`.** Moot while Quotient is unreachable from inside (area 7 revision). It would return only if Quotient became reachable and the organizers agreed (review A7.Q2); never the reset endpoint.
3. **The sinkhole** (review D76, D222). Deferred to the C2 fingerprinting lab: keep it only if first-bytes fingerprints discriminate; the code stays until then.
4. **Containerized scored services** (review N7.6). The 2027 stack is unverified; the Docker ecom variant is designed but unconfirmed.
5. **Generic restore onto a different host** (review A10.Q2) is tentative.
6. **The team Nextcloud** as the file-export path: expected writable from inside, unverified.
7. **Multiple viewers on one NETLAB console:** unknown; it decides how much of the team sees the one controller screen.
8. **Quotient's real configuration** (Delay, Jitter, Timeout, SLA threshold, Divisor, debug visibility, credlist count): measured at the Invitational.
9. **Per-module CPU and memory accounting** is self-reported; whether that is good enough is a lab question.
10. **Duplicate AD groups inject** (~500 groups across 10 departments, MW Discord 2026-10-26): whether Phylax should offer a read-only consolidation report.

## Known bugs to fix

Items 1 to 11 are from the 2026-10-31 review; items 12 to 23 were found while the module sections were written and reconciled with the core. Each is fixed in the owning module or core section's implementation, and T65 holds the regression tests.

1. **`kernel.module_block` Verify passes when the module is built in** (`internal/actions/linux_kmod.go:111-120`). It only compares the modprobe.d file. If `algif_aead` is compiled in, `linux.local_root_bundle` reports Copy Fail mitigated while it is not [[cert-cc-vulnerability-note-vu-260001#e6]]. Fix: probe `socket(AF_ALG)` bind to `aead`; if built in, use `initcall_blacklist=algif_aead_init` behind a reboot gate. Core (kernel family) and `hardening`.
2. **Rule id collision `D14`.** `rules/deps.yml:15,54,84` define `D14.new-dependency`, `D14b`, `D14c`, while D14 is network device tampering. Rename to `DEP1`-`DEP3`; add the rule-id registry check. `deps`.
3. **Stale Typst references** in v3 (cache tier 1, templates, complexity register, repo layout). The code uses fpdf (`docs/report.md`). Removed from v4; `report`, `depot`.
4. **Agent `fetch` handler is a no-op** (`internal/agent/handlers.go:41`). Depot and cache pulls cannot work. Core (wire).
5. **Placeholder step handler** rejects with "step execution not implemented" when `ExecConfig` is unset (`internal/agent/handlers.go:31,37`). Add a test that `phylax agent` always wires the real executor. Core (execution).
6. **Ledger alerts do not reach detection.** Rule D5d waits on a `binary_integrity` event nothing emits (`rules/pending/needs_producer.yml`). `integrity`.
7. **The controller never sends `freeze_capture`** for controller-scope `freeze_ring` collects (`docs/capture.md`). `capture`.
8. **Dead-man fires while connected are not reconciled until the next reconnect** (`docs/controller.md`). Core (execution).
9. **`plans/actions.yaml` header** still says "Each is a TODO" although the file has no stubs. Core.
10. **Reference `services.yml` lacks DNS and FTP**, both scored [[2027-mw-invitational-packet#e22]]. Core (manifest; the examples above add them).
11. **No `shortcut:` comments** anywhere although 70 `t.Skip` calls exist; known limits are not recorded. All modules.
12. **Sinkhole enabled in the reference `policy.yml` with no catcher, and the nat redirect bypasses the NFLOG deny log.** The 2027 reference has `sinkhole: { enabled: true, port: 7480 }`, but no catcher listener exists and nothing emits `net.sinkhole_capture`. In the current rendering the nat redirect at priority -100 sends denied TCP to loopback before the filter chain's deny-log rule sees it, so enabling it hides the denial from NFLOG and from `net.egress_denied`, the primary C2 signal (`internal/manifest/render/nft.go`, `internal/firewall/translate_linux.go`). Fix: the v4 `modules/egress.yml` block sets the sinkhole `false`; the redirect is reordered after the log or removed before anything turns it on, which the C2 fingerprinting lab (T60) decides. `egress`, `firewall`.
13. **Capture ring and freeze hold live in the Go heap against an 80 MB RSS footprint.** The code's ring (256 MiB) and hold (256 MiB) count against `debug.SetMemoryLimit` and `MemoryMax`; the core Footprint excluded "the packet ring". `policy.yml` still carries `packet_ring_max_bytes` and `packet_ring_free_pct`, which the code ignores. Fix: the Footprint now budgets the module's `ring_mb` and `hold_mb` on top of the 80 MB base; delete the dead policy fields. `capture`, core.
14. **Shadow would-drop rules share the deny NFLOG group.** A shadow-mode output policy logs would-drops to the same group as the enforced deny rule, so a would-drop also appears as `net.egress_denied`. Fix: a separate `shadow_log_group` and a `net.shadow_drop` kind. `firewall`, `net`.
15. **Sibling imports in the code.** `net` calls `deps.Collector` and emits `deps.edge` and `deps.peer` from its tracker; `internal/depot` imports `internal/integrity` for `Signer` and `Verifier`; `internal/depot/gotools` imports `internal/collect/net`. Fix: `deps` subscribes to `conn` and `listener`; `internal/signing` and `internal/sockets` become shared stateless libraries. `net`, `deps`, `depot`.
16. **The heartbeat does not carry the audit rules hash.** `Status` holds `RulesHash` and the verify loop emits `audit.rules_changed`, but nothing reads `Status()` into the heartbeat. Fix: `HealthReporter` and `Health.Info`. `audit`, core.
17. **Controller-origin module events are stored under the wrong agent, and some kinds are undeclared.** `wazuh` sets `Agent: "wazuh"`, `suricata` sets `"suricata"` or `"zeek"`; they must be agent `controller`. `net_connect` and `audit.rules_changed` are not declared with `event.Declare`; the old kind names are still used by rules and `internal/traceback/obs.go`. Fix: the retrofit renames the kinds in one go with the rename map (no alias layer). `wazuh`, `suricata`, `audit`, all modules.
18. **Honeytoken attribution rewrites stored alerts.** `Registry.Attribute` adds entities to incoming `detect.alert` events (`alerts.go`); stored events are hash-chained and are not rewritten. Fix: emit `honeytokens.sighting`. `honeytokens`.
19. **`icmp.iputils_pattern` is wrong for 64-bit iputils** (the pattern starts at byte 16, not 8, for a 16-byte timeval), so 56-byte pings report false (`docs/capture.md`). `capture`.
20. **The device health hook runs no scorer-mimic probe.** The adapters' health hook takes an `extra` function and every caller passes `nil`, so a Palo or VyOS commit is never probed inside its revert window. Fix: the executor's `Env.Probe` callback. `devices`, core.
21. **`depot` package actions need a patch window and a proxy, and declare no touches.** `pkg.install` and `pkg.upgrade` require the patch-window mode and an HTTP proxy, and `pkgScoredAliases` is a hard-coded list, so the scoring lint cannot see which service a package restarts. Fix: the `packages` list in `services.yml`. `depot`.
22. **The `ir_template` rule key survives in the loader and the corpus** although IR drafts come from the drafter by narrative (review D354). Delete it. `detect`.
23. **The reference `hosts.yml` gave the Windows hosts the `capture` role** although Windows capture is cut, so their health read `degraded` forever. Fixed in the reference manifest example of this design. Core (manifest).

### B. Linux persistence locations

Watched by `fim` and checked by the hunt:

- **Scheduling:** `/etc/crontab`, `/etc/cron.*/`, `/var/spool/cron/`, `/var/spool/at/`, systemd timers
- **systemd:** units in `/etc/systemd/system/`, `/usr/lib/systemd/system/`, user units, drop-ins, generators; unit `Environment=`, `AmbientCapabilities`, `CapabilityBoundingSet`
- **Boot:** `/etc/rc.local`, `/etc/init.d/`, `/etc/modules-load.d/`, `/etc/modprobe.d/`
- **Login and shell:** `/etc/profile`, `/etc/profile.d/`, `/etc/bash.bashrc`, `/etc/environment`, `/etc/inputrc`, per-user dotfiles including `.screenrc`, `.tmux.conf`, `.vimrc`, `.inputrc`; `/etc/update-motd.d/`, `~/.ssh/rc`, `/etc/ssh/sshrc`
- **Authentication:** `/etc/pam.d/`, PAM module directories, `pam_exec`, `/etc/nsswitch.conf` and NSS libraries, all `authorized_keys`, plus `AuthorizedKeysFile` and `AuthorizedKeysCommand`
- **Accounts:** `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/group`, `/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/sudoers.d/`
- **Loader:** `/etc/ld.so.preload`, `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/`, `LD_PRELOAD` in service environments, `/proc/<pid>/maps` of services
- **Package hooks and holds:** apt `Pre-Invoke` and `Post-Invoke`, dnf plugins, `apt-mark hold`, `versionlock.list`
- **Device events:** `/etc/udev/rules.d/`
- **Log rotation:** `/etc/logrotate.d/` postrotate scripts
- **Web:** `php.ini` and `conf.d` (`auto_prepend_file`, `auto_append_file`, `disable_functions`, `extension=`), PHP `extension_dir`, `.htaccess`, Apache modules and `Include` lines
- **Mail:** Postfix `master.cf` and content filters, `/etc/aliases` command pipes, Dovecot post-login and global sieve
- **Database:** MySQL UDFs (`mysql.func`), plugin directory, `mysql.user`, application admin tables
- **Kernel:** loaded modules, BPF programs, module-loading state
- **Privilege:** SUID and SGID files, file capabilities, immutable and append-only attributes
- **Mounts:** bind, overlay and tmpfs mounts over content and persistence directories
- **Splunk:** `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps`, scripted inputs, `outputs.conf`, deployment-server settings
- **Desktop:** XDG autostart on workstations

### C. Windows persistence locations

- Scheduled tasks (including GPO-deployed), with content review and the `\Microsoft\` folder
- Services (binary path, `ServiceDll`, failure actions), including unsigned SYSTEM services and masquerade names
- Run, RunOnce and RunServices keys (HKLM, HKCU, WOW6432Node); startup folders
- Winlogon `Userinit`, `Shell`, `Notify`; AppInit_DLLs; AppCertDlls
- Image File Execution Options (`Debugger`, `GlobalFlag`); SilentProcessExit
- LSA Security, Authentication and Notification packages
- WMI event filters, consumers and bindings
- Netsh helpers, print monitors, time providers, Winsock providers
- COM hijacks under `HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID`
- BITS jobs
- IIS native and managed modules, handlers, ISAPI filters, FTP roots on UNC paths
- DNS `ServerLevelPluginDll`, forwarders and zones on the DC
- Accessibility binaries (`sethc.exe`, `utilman.exe`, `osk.exe`) replaced or redirected
- PowerShell profiles (all scopes)
- Accounts: hidden accounts ending in `$`, RID hijacking, Guest enabled, nested privileged groups
- AD: GPOs and SYSVOL, AdminSDHolder, delegation, SID history, `gPLink`
- Optional features: WSL, OpenSSH server, VNC, Chocolatey, remote-access tools
- SQL Server: `xp_cmdshell`, Agent jobs, linked servers, startup procedures


### D. Repository layout

#### Two repositories

The `phylax` repository holds the product: the binary, its modules, the content they load, the manifest schema and reference manifests, the documentation and the signed-release fallback. The red team can read it (an adversary assumption in the trust model), so it holds nothing that helps them beyond what the source already shows.

The lab, Terraform, Packer and red-team material live in a separate private repo (`ccdc-lab`) and never in `phylax` (review D521). The reason is exposure, not any rule: campaign runbooks, the contaminator's implant sets (defanged but real), exploit and emulation notes, lab scorer configs and the replica topology would tell an attacker what we test against. The replica's VM definitions are built in `btap-infra` (branch `ccdc27-lab`). The team knowledge base (research, strategy, packets, evidence cards) is `ccdc-private`, a vault, not a code repo.

#### The tree

```text
phylax/                          # public product repo
  cmd/phylax/                    # the one binary: serve, agent, init, cache, rules, ledger, set-controller,
                                 #   modules, depot, tools, guard, say, claim, creds sheet, bench, agent rollback
  internal/
    event/  module/              # envelope and typed events; the module contract and registry
    module/conformance/          # the shared conformance suite (run against every registered module in CI)
    agent/  agent/mods/          # agent mode: supervisor, factories, exec; one registration file per agent module
    link/  spool/  store/        # core: TLS pinning and framing; crash-safe spool; SQLite store and query API
    vault/  manifest/  plan/     # core: secrets; manifest types and schema; plan and config types
    actions/  deadman/           # core: the action framework and general families; dead-man journal
    controller/                  # core: host for controller modules; plan engine glue; agent config rendering
    ui/                          # core: UI shell, registrar, templates, vendored htmx
    svcinstall/  atomicfile/     # core helpers: service install; atomic writes
    enroll/                      # core: first contact and enrollment (SSH and WinRM push, one-liner, bootstrap handler, tokens, set-controller)
    bench/                       # core: comms bench (histograms, JSONL recorder, report, load generator under bench/load/)
    manifest/render/             # core: renderers from the manifest to firewall policy, agent configs and plan targets
    parsers/                     # shared protocol parsers, one package each (incl. smb2, winrm, tds, ssh)
    sockets/  signing/           # shared stateless libraries: sock_diag and inode join; release-key Signer and Verifier
    # one package per module (agent side, controller side or both):
    audit/  winevt/  net/  logs/  inventory/   # logs/parsers/ and inventory/{probes,software}/ are embedded content inside these packages
    # shared stateless library subpackages inside module trees (the closed list is in the module contract):
    #   checks/probe (the probe library and protocol clients: ntlm, smb, winrm, ssh, mssql, ldap, web),
    #   integrity/format (ledger and package-database readers), inventory/fold (snapshot plus rows to rows)
    detect/  respond/  content_guard/
    integrity/  hunt/  hardening/  ad/
    firewall/  egress/  capture/  devices/  devices/palo/  devices/vyos/
    checks/  scorer/  vantage/  creds/
    traceback/  chains/  deps/  vuln/
    decoys/  honeytokens/
    report/  backup/  teamfeed/  notify/
    depot/  wazuh/  splunk/  suricata/
    e2e/                         # end-to-end tests (the relay test T47 lives here)
  manifest/
    schema/                      # JSON Schema, generated from the Go structs
    2027/                        # the reference manifest (topology, hosts, services, accounts, scorer, devices, ...)
    2027/modules/                # one <name>.yml per module block: the core-default set enabled per host OS and role, plus the opt-in modules the game-day order uses (inventory, and backup on servers)
    two-segment/                 # the multi-segment variant (relays); it reuses 2027/modules/ except for the relay settings
  rules/<module>/                # detection rules per owning module (rules/detect/, rules/respond/, rules/chains/, ...),
                                 #   rules/lists.yml, rules/profiles.yml, rules/ported/ (hand-ported packs), rules/yara/ (the corpus,
                                 #   including the MIT-licensed UCF rules); rules/pending/ for rules waiting on a producer
  plans/<module>/                # plan templates per owning module (plans/hardening/ with the first-hour library, plans/backup/,
                                 #   plans/creds/, plans/hunt/, plans/ad/, ...)
  checks/                        # active check content: checks/checks/, checks/flows/ (Orange flows), checks/doctor/
  reports/                       # the report module's content: generators/, queries/, evidence/, lint.yml
  hunt/                          # hunt content: checks/, killlist.yml, heuristics.yml, baselines/
  ledger/                        # signed ledger indexes shipped in the release
  ad/                            # AD check definitions and default service descriptors
  backups/counts/                # record-count specifications per service kind
  pools/                         # decoy banners, honey filenames, fake-shell content
  depot/                         # recipes and tools.json: the trusted tool depot's index sources
  inject-kit/                    # the memo shell only (inject-kit/memo.md.tmpl); no policies, plans or drafts
  dist/                          # signed binaries, fallback delivery
  docs/                          # implementation notes (docs/*.md), the impl briefs and the review (docs/impl/)
  .github/workflows/             # CI: build, size, vet, race, privileged job, conformance, content tests
  Makefile  mise.toml  AGENTS.md go.mod go.sum
  THIRD_PARTY_RULES.md           # generated: hand-ported rules with upstream id, path, commit, author, licence

ccdc-lab/                        # private, never declared or published
  terraform/  packer/  netem/  proxy/
  reference/                     # baseline and ledger builders
  quotient/                      # lab scorer config, stand-in check scripts
  sim/orange/  sim/contaminator/  sim/faults/   # sim/orange runs the checks module's Orange flows from many sources
  redteam/                       # campaigns 01 to 09, results, the C2 fingerprinting corpus
```

#### What changed from v3

- **Module packages replace topic packages.** Each module is one package under `internal/`, named for the module. Today's `internal/collect/{audit,net,winevt}` become `internal/audit`, `internal/net` and `internal/winevt` in the retrofit; `internal/integrations` splits into `internal/wazuh`, `internal/splunk` and `internal/suricata`; the scorer's round clock, discovery, fingerprints, SLA and PCR code split between `scorer` and `creds`.
- **New core packages:** `internal/enroll` (first contact and enrollment, builder check), `internal/bench` (the comms bench), `internal/manifest/render`, `internal/module` (the manifest, health and host interfaces, `module.Common`) and `internal/module/conformance`, plus the shared stateless libraries `internal/sockets` and `internal/signing` and the library subpackages `checks/probe`, `integrity/format` and `inventory/fold`.
- **Content directories per module.** Today's flat `rules/*.yml` and `plans/*.yaml` move under their owning module's directory (`rules/detect/`, `plans/hardening/`) as that module is retrofitted. A content file names its module and loads only when the module is enabled on the target.
- **`internal/cache` is gone.** The depot module holds the content-addressed cache and its sync client; `phylax cache` and `phylax depot` are its commands.
- **No Typst.** `inject-kit/` holds one memo shell; the policies, plans, risk register, framework templates and pre-written drafts are cut and live outside Phylax (decision 6). PDFs come from the pure-Go renderer in `internal/report`.
- **No `rules/imported/`.** The Sigma importer is cut; third-party logic is hand-ported into `rules/<module>/` with a `source:` record and listed in `THIRD_PARTY_RULES.md`.
- **No `phylax doctor`.** The `hello` capabilities block and the Platform page replace it; `phylax modules` lists the manifests.
- **`manifest/2027/modules/`** replaces v3's catch-all `policy.yml`; `decoys.yml` and `integrations.yml` are gone and their content lives in the owning modules' blocks.
- **`reports/`** is new: the generators, saved queries, evidence recipes and lint data of the `report` module are content, not Go.

Review rows carried by the appendices (traceability; the row text is in `docs/impl/review.md`): review D518 (Appendix A: Windows event reference; KEEP); review D519 ((see docs/impl/review.md)); review D520 ((see docs/impl/review.md)); review D522 (Appendix G: scorer fingerprint table per layer; KEEP); review D533 (Rule backlog P01-P81, each becomes a tested file when producer and fixture exist; KEEP).

### E. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Action | A typed, Go-native operation with check, apply, verify and rollback |
| Plan | A DAG of actions on specific targets, with dependencies and approval gates |
| Dead-man switch | Rollback that fires on the agent unless it re-establishes its link after a risky change |
| Relay | An agent role that splices its segment's connections to the controller |
| Fact | A typed cross-host value the controller sends to agents in a signed `control: fact` message; the agent bus sees it as a `controller.fact` event, and an absent or expired fact is unknown |
| Standing approval | An operator's one-time approval of a plan template, targets and actions with an expiry, so scheduled work can run without a click each time |
| Controller executor | The part of `phylax serve` that runs actions with no host to run on (device adapters, depot fetches, integration helpers), under the same action contract |
| Device proxy | An agent role that splices the controller to a network device's management interface |
| Spool | The agent's crash-safe, sequenced, hash-chained local store of events awaiting acknowledgment |
| Active check | Our own end-to-end test of a service, managed in the UI |
| Scorer-mimic probe | An active check that reproduces Quotient's exact transport for one service |
| Faithful sample, union sweep | The two modes of an active check: one random item and credential as the scorer does, and every learned item |
| Burst, round | One scorer pass over every service; rounds start `Delay ± Jitter` apart |
| PCR | Quotient's password change request: CSV `username,password`, effective immediately in Quotient; entered by a human outside the environment |
| Credlist | A named list of scored accounts in Quotient; PCR uses its path |
| Discovered check | A check the scorer was observed running, proposed as an active check |
| Trace-back | The chain from a change back to the request and source that caused it |
| Hop, chain, campaign | One step of an intrusion; an ordered list of hops; chains merged by shared source, account, hash or C2 |
| Integrity ledger | Reference hashes with provenance used to judge binaries and libraries; alert only |
| Depot | Local known-good copies of binaries and packages used for restores |
| Vantage point | A place from which checks run: an in-LAN `check_runner` (the controller host's is the reference) or the Kali |
| Community ID | A hash of a flow's endpoints that joins records across tools |
| Honeytoken | A fake credential, key or path, unique per host, whose use reveals where it was stolen |
| Tier 0, 1, 2 | Response levels (A-AUTO): automatic behind probes, rollback and breakers; one-click; manual with checklist |
| Auto class | Plan approval class `auto` (A-AUTO): a plan from a module's allowlist that the controller signs itself when its conditions hold; a failed condition makes it a click proposal |
| Safe mode | Global switch that suspends automatic responses and plan execution |

### G. Scorer fingerprint table (Quotient at commit `9000379`)

Library versions follow the Go and module versions of whatever build runs at the event; re-learn the hashes each event [Q §6].

| Layer | Observed behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Timing | A burst of about 15 SYNs per team per box within 25–55 ms every `Delay ± Jitter`; all teams in the same sub-second window |
| SSH | Banner is one of 27 strings; KEXINIT is constant (HASSH `a7230c16…` for the real login, `0a07365c…` for `BadAttempts` logins); `none` then `password`; `pty-req xterm 40x80`; `shell`; one typed line; about 1.3 s dwell; `Failed password` immediately followed by `Accepted password` from the same runner |
| HTTP | `GET`, `Host: ip:port` with the port, a random old User-Agent (a non-signal), `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, `Connection: close`, nothing else |
| TLS | Go ClientHello, no SNI, no ALPN, about 1.5 KB; JA4 `t13i131000_f57a46bbacb6_ab7e3b40a677` for Go 1.25 |
| DNS | A (or MX) question, RD set, no EDNS, random id and port; a duplicate query on deadline |
| ICMP | go-ping, 24-byte payload, seq 0, random id |
| SMTP | `EHLO localhost`, `AUTH PLAIN`, `MAIL FROM:<u> BODY=8BITMIME`, `RCPT TO:<other user>`, 16-hex subject, 64-hex body |
| IMAP, POP3, FTP | IMAP: 6-character tag, `LOGIN`, `LIST "" "*"`, `LOGOUT`. POP3: `USER`, `PASS`, `NOOP`, `STAT`. FTP: `USER`, `PASS`, `FEAT`, `TYPE I`, `OPTS UTF8 ON`, `EPSV`, `RETR`, `QUIT` |
| SMB | Negotiate, NTLM (flags `0xe2888215`, no Seal), tree `\\ip:445\share`, the domain in AUTH is the server's own name |
| WinRM | `POST /wsman`, `Go-http-client/1.1`, SOAP shell-create first without Authorization |
| RDP, tcp | Handshake, zero payload, held open 6 ms to 100 s with keepalives |
| Custom (MSSQL, Splunk, RDP-with-auth) | Script-defined; label by burst, port and account only |

### I. Rule backlog

The 81 proposed rules [PR] group as: credentials and accounts (P01–P05, P14–P16), Zerologon and AD (P06, P62–P64, P68–P69), local-root and exposure (P07–P09), web and database (P10–P11, P39–P42, P44, P48–P49), Linux persistence and evasion (P12–P13, P17–P25, P27–P32, P38), integrity and masquerade (P26, P60–P61), network and covert channels (P33–P35, P45, P73–P74, P79), services and sabotage (P50–P53, P75–P78), Windows persistence (P43, P46–P47, P54–P59), defense evasion (P65–P67), devices (P70–P72), and re-infection and hardware (P80–P81). Each ships when its producer exists and its fixture passes.

### J. Removed in v4

One line per capability v3 had that v4 drops, with the reason. Cut code is deleted; git history is the archive (decision 2). Review ids in parentheses.

**Cut rows:**

- `phylax doctor` capability probe (D20): duplicate of the `hello` capabilities block and the Platform page; one probe, shown in the UI.
- Patch proxy module `patch_proxy` (D84, D217): a new listener and protocol to maintain; packages install from the depot over `fetch`, plus a time-boxed egress allowance for misses.
- ALPN `phylax/patch` (D112): goes with the patch proxy.
- Proc connector cross-check and divergence alerts (D89): the code chose audit over netlink plus `sock_diag`; one exec source is the norm.
- Optional eBPF exec sensor (D92): audit is the chosen path and a kernel rootkit blinds audit and eBPF alike; reopen only if the exec-storm test (T43) fails.
- Sigma importer `phylax rules import-sigma` (D314): no code, about 98 hand rules exist, and an importer is a compiler to maintain; hand-port the rules we want.
- Sigma-derived scheduled searches on Splunk (D318): duplicates on-host detection; bulk Sigma searches were unusable at the one team that tried.
- `hunt.pii` personal-data scan (D404): no evidence it scores.
- Windows raw-socket capture with `SIO_RCVALL` (D235): unbuilt and unreliable; Windows network coverage comes from Sysmon 3, 5156/5157 and Palo logs.
- Kerberos metadata parsing and file carving from HTTP, FTP and SMB (D242): no evidence it scores or speeds an IR; Sysmon and DC events cover Kerberos.
- Decoys on public addresses (D389): the organizer's perimeter assessment scores extraneous services, so public decoys lose points; decoys stay inside the LAN.
- Pre-written inject drafts (D491): decision 6, no prewritten inject responses.
- Session recording (D10): no design and no code; the action audit trail covers what we need, and no peer credits recordings with a win.
- ClamAV on Windows (D441): Defender is already there and protected by tier 0.
- Offline bundle collection mode (N3.5): simplicity (A4.Q3); the console one-liner already covers unreachable hosts.
- Exec-time YARA gate on `FAN_OPEN_EXEC_PERM` (N5.10): a hung permission event blocks exec on a scored host (A5.Q3).
- ModSecurity plus CRS plan (N5.11): simplicity, and turning the engine on can fail scored web checks (A5.Q3).
- Event archive and export (N11.2): Phylax cannot reach the portals; records live outside Phylax (area 11 answer).
- Inject tracker and board (D480): inject tracking is out of scope (area 11 answer).

**Parts removed from kept rows:**

- `modules.disable_loading` action (D157): unused; `kernel.modules_disabled` is one-way and does nothing against prebaked modules (A2.Q3, A3.Q2).
- Detection rules D19 promiscuous NIC and D20 allowed-protocol abuse (D339): no evidence red used them against us.
- Kali NAT-behaviour, blocked-source and Palo-load probes (D379): no evidence they score.
- Splunk REST parser (D241): the check and logs cover it.
- IIS templates, request linking and reference checks (D163, D289, D400): IIS is not in the 2027 environment.
- Policy, plan, risk-register and framework inject templates (D490): decision 6; one memo shell stays as a generator.
- NISE upload integration (D489): a human uploads in a browser; the Nextcloud fallback becomes the file-export path.
- Typed regex parameters for pre-approved `host.exec` tools (D85): simplicity (A4.Q3).
- Dropbear host-key regeneration in `net.vyos_review` (D531): simplicity (A5.Q3).
- Rule-format `macros:`, `maturity:` and `requires:` (D306-D311): simplicity (A4.Q3).
- Quotient portal poll, pasted credlists and pasted Up/Down table as primary inputs (D278-D280): Quotient is unreachable from inside; an optional hand-entered Up/Down note remains.
- `pcr.submit` (D430, D167): PCRs are entered by a human outside the environment.
- `av.clamav` integration action (D168): goes with D441.
- Typst in the cache, templates and controller (D442-D445, D490; Known bug 3): decision 7, pure-Go PDF.
- Four cache tiers (D442-D445): one signed index with a priority field.
- In-process kernel-memory accounting (D67): enforce through systemd and the Job Object; report kernel-held memory only.
- Agent-only build tag (D66): deferred in v3 round 4 and not needed.
- Separate Integrations and Cache UI pages (D475, D476): folded into the Platform page.
- Separate Egress and C2 page (D470): folded into the Traffic page.
- Printed per-role checklists as the primary form (D503): replaced by the host x step grid; print is the fallback.
- Separate `crossview` and `scan` agent modules (D80, D83): their checks are hunt content and `integrity` work.
- Process-connector leg of the cross-source tripwires (D103): goes with D89.
- Sinkhole leg of rule D13 (D333): pending the C2 fingerprinting lab.
- Campaign merge as the unit of an IR (D304): a view only; one IR per narrative or persistence mechanism.
- `rotation: pcr_transaction` for all mail users (D195): no mass rotation.
- `sysadmin` protected until the PCR list says otherwise (D433): no admin accounts are scored.
- Account-guessing inference in scorer-account learning: never built as a separate path; learning from observed logins stays (area 7 revision).
